posts.post_content:
Botterverse is where you build AI chatbots, share them and sell them. The member area is called Botter's Lab.

What you can do

  • Build a bot from your own instructions and files, on the AI model you choose.
  • Share it by a link or put it on your own website.
  • Sell access to it with a one-time paywall.
  • Trade bots with other members on Bot Market.
  • Refer new members and earn commission through the affiliate programme.

What you can use depends on your plan. See Plans and what each one unlocks.

How messages are paid for

Every message a bot sends uses credits. Your plan includes credits each month and you can buy more. As the bot's owner you pay for the chats your visitors have with it, including your own testing. See What credits are.

Good bots only

Every bot is checked before it can go Public. Some kinds of bot are not allowed at all. Others are allowed but must say what they do on their Certified by Botterverse page. See Declarations.

Bot Market is for members

Bot Market is where members buy and sell bots with each other. It is not a store for the public. Your own customers reach your bots through your link, your website or your own promotion.

Where to start

  • Create your first bot and publish it
  • The member menu

One account does everything: building, buying and selling.

Create your account

  1. Open the Create your account page.
  2. Choose a Username. It becomes part of the url your bots are served at and the name you sign in with. It cannot be changed later, so choose with care.
  3. Fill in First name, Last name, Email address, Password and Password again.
  4. Choose your Country from the list. If we cannot pay earnings to that country yet, a note says so. You can still register, build bots and buy.
  5. Tick the box to accept the terms and conditions and the privacy policy. Both are linked beside it and open in a new tab.
  6. Press Create my account.

Confirm your email address

We email you a link. Until you open it, some things stay closed, such as making a bot Public or submitting a listing. If the email has not arrived, press Send it again.

Choose a plan

There is no free plan and no free trial. Every plan is a paid subscription, bought on the pricing page of the Botterverse website.

  • Buy it with the same email address you signed up with. If you buy first, register for Botter's Lab with the email address you bought with. That is how the payment is matched to your account.
  • After you buy, expect one email from the purchase with two links: one sets the password of your billing login and one creates your Botter's Lab account with the same email address. See Invoices, receipts and saved cards for the billing login.
  • If you paid before you had an account, the banner Verify your email to activate your plan shows until you confirm your email. Your plan and its credits are then added.
  • With no plan, Billing and credits says You have no plan yet and offers See the plans.

See Plans and what each one unlocks.

Sign in

You sign in with your Username and Password, never your email address. Tick Keep me signed in on a device you trust. The eye button in its own section at the end of the Password field shows or hides what you typed.

If you forget your details

On the sign-in page Forgotten username? sits at the right of the Username label and Forgotten password? at the right of the Password label.

  • Forgotten password?: enter your username and we send a link to choose a new password to the email on your account.
  • Forgotten username?: enter your email address and we send your username to it.

Paying from the EU

Nobody in the EU can pay for anything on Botterverse: a plan, credits, bot access or a Bot Market purchase. A visitor from the EU sees Not available in your country at a pay step. Free Public bots still work for them.

The Dashboard is the first page you see after signing in. It shows how things stand at a glance.

The three figures

  • Credit balance: the whole credits you have left to spend.
  • Usage this month: the messages across all of your bots this month.
  • Active bots: your running bots against your plan's bot limit, such as "3 of 5". The line under it says how many are paused. Paused bots count towards the limit too, so you can be at the limit with fewer running bots than it allows. If your plan has no limit, the line says so.

Revenue over time

A graph of your share of the sales of all of your bots. Change the period with the Date range control: Last week, Last month, Year to date, Last 5 years or Custom range.

Your bots

Each bot is listed with its status, such as Running or Paused by you. Select a bot to open its Bot analytics.

No bots yet

With no bots, the page invites you to build one. Press New bot to start. See Create your first bot and publish it.

posts.post_title: Plans and what each one unlocks
posts.post_content:
There are five plans. Each one includes everything in the plan before it. Prices, bot limits and included credits are on the pricing page of the Botterverse website, since they can change.

Apprentice Botter

  • Build bots and share them by link or embed.
  • Everyday AI models. The most expensive model from each provider is not offered.
  • Buy bots on Bot Market.
  • Your bot pages carry the default look.

Not included: the paywall, integrations, analytics panels, the affiliate programme and selling on Bot Market.

Novice Botter

Adds:

  • More bots.
  • Every AI model.
  • The paywall with message top-ups.
  • Integrations.
  • Basic analytics.
  • The affiliate programme.

Expert Botter

Adds more bots, larger included credits and deeper analytics: busiest hours, top conversation starters and category benchmarks.

Pro Botter

Adds:

  • More bots again.
  • Bot styles, with a powered-by tag you can remove.
  • A lower platform fee on your sales.
  • Selling on Bot Market and your own licence terms.
  • The CRM connector.
  • Priority support.

Master Botter

Adds A/B tests and advanced analytics, which set views against purchases.

How to see what your plan includes

  • Your plan's name shows under your name at the top right.
  • A page your plan does not include shows a short note in place of its content. The note says what the feature does and which plans include it, with a Change plan or See your plan button.
  • The Dashboard shows your bot limit under Active bots.

Credits and your plan

Each plan includes credits every month. Unused included credits expire at the next renewal or plan change. Credits you buy never expire. See What credits are.

Buying a plan

Plans are bought on the pricing page of the Botterverse website.

  • Register for Botter's Lab with the email address you bought with, before or after you buy. That is how your plan is added to your account.
  • After you buy, expect one email from the purchase with two links. The first sets the password of your billing login, where you see invoices, change your card or cancel. The second creates your Botter's Lab account with the same email address.
  • Already have a Botter's Lab account under that email? Sign in and verify your email if you have not yet. Your plan is then added automatically.

See Invoices, receipts and saved cards for the billing login.

Changing plan

See Change your plan.

The menu runs down the left of the screen. On a phone it is folded away: press the menu button at the top left to open it.

The menu

Dashboard sits at the top. Below it the pages are grouped.

Bots

  • Bot list: every bot you own. The Bot builder opens from here.
  • Import a bot: build a bot from instructions you already have.
  • Analytics: figures for each bot.
  • A/B tests: test two versions of a bot (Master Botter).
  • Bot styles: the look of your bots' own pages (Pro Botter and above).

Bot Market

  • Browse: bots other members have listed for sale.
  • Bots I bought: other members' bots you bought paid access to.
  • My listings: your bots on sale (Pro Botter and above).
  • My profile: your public seller profile.

Earnings

  • Sales: every sale of your bots.
  • Payouts: your earnings and withdrawals.

Account

  • Billing and credits: credits, auto top-up, credit packs and your plan.

At the foot of the menu:

  • Settings: your account, email notifications, branding, CRM and licence terms.
  • Support: opens the Botter Support Team's help desk in a new tab.
  • Help: opens these help pages in a new tab.
  • Feedback: opens the Feedback page in a new tab, to report a bug or suggest an idea. See Report a bug or suggest an idea.
  • Affiliates: the affiliate programme (Novice Botter and above).

Support, Help and Feedback are on the Botterverse website, so each carries a small arrow that shows it opens in a new tab.

Every entry shows whatever your plan. A page your plan does not include tells you which plans have it.

The bar at the top

From left to right on the right-hand side:

  • A red status pill, shown only when your account needs you to act, such as Payment past due or Plan cancelling. See Account status messages.
  • Your credits: your balance in whole credits. Press it to open Billing and credits.
  • The theme button: a moon or a sun. It switches between the light Pleasant Pink theme and the dark Nightshift theme.
  • Your name and plan: opens a menu with Settings, Billing and credits and Sign out.

Banners

A banner across the top of the page asks you to act on something, such as accepting updated terms or confirming your email address. It stays until you have done it.

A new bot starts Personal, so only you can use it until you make it Public.

Steps

  1. Open Bot list in the menu.
  2. Press New bot. The Bot builder opens with the title New bot.
  3. Open Details and give the bot a Name. Add a Description if you like.
  4. Open Instructions and write what the bot should do. See Write the instructions.
  5. Press Save in the bar at the foot of the screen.

The bot is now in your Bot list. Some sections only work once the bot is saved: knowledge files, integrations, the mode and the preview.

Next

  • Add knowledge files
  • Preview your bot
  • Make it Public

If you cannot create a bot

Every bot you own counts towards your plan's bot limit, whether it is Personal or Public, running or paused, built or bought. At the limit the New bot button is hidden and a note says You are at your plan's bot limit. Change your plan to add more bots. Delete a bot you no longer need or change your plan.

Already have a bot elsewhere?

Use Import a bot to paste in its instructions and files. See Import a bot.

posts.post_title: The Bot builder and its sections
posts.post_content:
The Bot builder holds everything about one bot on one page. Open it from Bot list by pressing a bot's name or Edit.

Every section starts folded. Press a section's heading to open it. On a wide screen a list of sections sits beside them, so you can jump to one. On a phone use the Jump to menu above the sections.

The sections, in order

  1. Details: the name, description and image. The image is a jpg, png or webp file.
  2. Category: how the bot is grouped. See Starters and category.
  3. Instructions: what the bot knows and how it behaves. See Write the instructions.
  4. Conversation starters: prompts shown to new visitors.
  5. Knowledge files: files the bot can draw on. See Knowledge files.
  6. Model: the AI model the bot runs on. See Choose a model.
  7. Mode: Personal or Public, with the declarations. See Personal and Public.
  8. Paywall and pricing: sell access to the bot. See The paywall.
  9. Style: the bot style its pages use (Pro Botter and above). See Bot styles.
  10. Integrations: services the bot can call. See Integrations.

Then the Advanced sections:

  1. Sharing and embed: the share link, the embed snippet, Require visitors to sign up and the Daily credit limit. See Share your bot.
  2. Interest tags: the CRM interest tag rules that cover this bot (Pro Botter and above). See Interest tags.
  3. Preview: chat with the bot as a visitor would. See Preview your bot.
  4. Analytics: messages this month, the bot's status, a link to Full analytics and the Conversation insights switch.

Saving

Most fields are kept only when you press Save. A few actions take effect at once. See Saving and actions that take effect now.

At the foot of the page

Duplicate, Pause or Unpause and Delete. See Duplicate, pause or delete a bot.

A bot you bought

On a bot you hold on Personal use, Resell rights or Master resell rights, the Instructions and Knowledge files sections are not shown. The name, description, category and starters can be read but not changed. The model, integrations, style, mode and paywall stay yours to set, as the licence allows. A PLR bot can be renamed and edited. See Bots you bought on Bot Market.

The instructions tell the bot who it is, what it knows and how to behave. You write them in plain language. No code is needed.

Steps

  1. In the Bot builder, open Instructions.
  2. Type in the box What the bot should do.
  3. Press Save.

What to include

  • Who the bot is for and what it helps with.
  • The tone it should take, such as friendly or formal.
  • What it should not do or talk about.
  • How to use its knowledge files, if it has any.
  • What to say when it does not know the answer.

Limits

The instructions share the model's space with the bot's knowledge and the visitor's message. If they are too long for the model, Save refuses them with The instructions are too large for this model, which leaves no room for knowledge and a message. Shorten them. Shorten them or choose another model.

Your instructions stay private

Every bot is told never to reveal, quote, summarise or translate its instructions or knowledge files, whatever a visitor asks.

Every saved version is kept

Each time you save, the instructions are kept as a new version.

On a Public bot

Saving a change to a Public bot runs the safety check again. See The publish check.

Conversation starters

Starters are suggested first messages. Visitors see them when they open the bot, so they know what to ask. They also show on the paywall under Things you can ask it.

  1. In the Bot builder, open Conversation starters.
  2. Press Add a starter and type it.
  3. Repeat for each starter. Press Remove beside one to take it away.
  4. Press Save.

Bot analytics counts how often each starter opens a conversation, under Top conversation starters (Expert Botter and above).

Category

The category groups the bot. Buyers browse Bot Market by category and the category benchmarks on Bot analytics compare your bot with others in it.

  1. Open Category.
  2. Choose one from the Category list. No category is allowed for a bot you do not plan to sell.
  3. Or press Suggest a category. The suggestion appears beside the button, such as "Suggested: Marketing. Save to keep it." Suggestions use no credits.
  4. Press Save.

A bot needs a category before it can be listed on Bot Market.

Knowledge files are your own material for the bot to answer from, such as a product guide, a price list or a set of notes.

What you can upload

The section shows how many files a bot can hold, the largest size of each file and the file types allowed. These are PDF, Word, text, Markdown and CSV. Uploading uses no credits.

Add a file

  1. Save the bot first. A new bot shows Save the bot first, then add files to it.
  2. Open Knowledge files.
  3. Under Add a file, press Browse and choose the file.
  4. Press Upload.

The file shows Being read while it is prepared, then Ready. Only a ready file is used.

Uploading and deleting a file take effect now, without Save.

A file that cannot be read

If the file shows This file could not be read. Try another copy of it., save it again from the app that made it or as a different type. Then upload the new copy. A file larger than the limit is refused before it is sent.

Delete a file

Press Delete beside the file and confirm. The bot stops using it at once and this cannot be undone.

How the bot uses large knowledge

When a bot's knowledge fits, all of it is sent with each message. When there is more than fits, the bot sends the passages that best match each message, so a large library still works.

Open a file

Press a file's name to open the file you uploaded.

A bot you bought

On a bot held below PLR the Knowledge files section is not shown.

Each bot runs on one AI model. There are four families: Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok. Claude is the default.

Steps

  1. In the Bot builder, open Model.
  2. Choose from the Model list.
  3. Press Save.

Which models you see

  • Apprentice Botter offers the everyday models. Novice Botter and above offer every model.
  • A model with no price in force is not offered.

Cost

A more expensive model uses more credits per message. A cheaper model lets your credits go further. Try the bot in Preview after a change to see how it answers.

When a change is refused

  • The instructions are too large for this model: shorten the instructions or choose a model with more room.
  • This model is not available to you. Choose another model.: the model is not offered on your plan or no longer offered for new choices.
  • An A/B test that is a draft or running has variant instructions too large for the new model: change the test first.

When a model is withdrawn

A model can be withdrawn for new bots while bots already on it keep working. If a model is fully retired, a bot on it stops answering until you choose another model.

On a Public bot

A change of model means confirming the bot's declarations again. See Declarations.

Chat with your bot inside the Bot builder before anyone else sees it.

Steps

  1. Save the bot. A new bot shows Save the bot first, then chat with it here.
  2. Open Preview, under Advanced.
  3. Type a message or press one of your conversation starters.

Good to know

  • The preview uses the instructions, knowledge, model and integrations you last saved. Press Save before testing a change.
  • Preview messages use your credits, like any other message.
  • The visitor limits do not apply to you, in the preview or on your bot's own page.
  • Works on a Personal bot, so you can test in private.

posts.post_title: Saving and actions that take effect now
posts.post_content:
Nothing you type in the Bot builder reaches your visitors until you press Save. Half-finished edits stay with you.

The Save bar

The bar at the foot of the screen stays in view as you scroll. It says:

  • This bot is not saved yet. for a new bot.
  • Unsaved changes as soon as you change a field.
  • All changes are saved. once you have saved.

Press Save to keep your changes. The message The bot is saved. confirms it. If a field is refused, its section opens and shows why.

What Save keeps

The name, description, image, category, instructions, starters, model, paywall settings, style, Require visitors to sign up, Daily credit limit and the Conversation insights switch.

What takes effect now, without Save

These act as soon as you press them. Each one says "takes effect now" beside it.

  • Changing the mode: Make Public and Switch back to Personal.
  • Confirm declarations.
  • Uploading and deleting a knowledge file.
  • Adding, editing, switching on or off and removing an integration.
  • Duplicate, Pause, Unpause and Delete.

Saving a Public bot

Every saved change to a Public bot runs the safety check again. See The publish check.

posts.post_title: Duplicate, pause or delete a bot
posts.post_content:
These buttons are on each bot in Bot list and at the foot of the Bot builder. Each takes effect now, without Save.

Duplicate

Duplicate makes a copy of the bot, with "Copy" added to its name. Use it to try a new idea without touching a bot that works.

  • The copy starts Personal with its paywall off.
  • It keeps the instructions, knowledge files, starters, model and integrations, with their credentials.
  • It counts towards your bot limit.
  • A bought bot keeps its licence and the name it arrived with.

A bot bought on Bot Market cannot be duplicated until its refund window has passed or you have put it on sale. The builder says so in place of the button.

Pause and unpause

Pause stops a running bot answering. Visitors see a message that the bot is not available. Press Unpause to run it again.

A paused bot still counts towards your bot limit. A bot paused for another reason has no Unpause button:

  • Paused by the Botter Support Team: only they can unpause it. Contact them through Support.
  • Paused by your plan: see Your Bot list.
  • Paused for account closing: reopen your account to run it again.

Delete

  1. Press Delete.
  2. Read the box Delete this bot?. It says what happens to this bot.
  3. Press Delete bot to go ahead or Keep it to stop.

What happens depends on the bot's history:

  • A bot that has never been shared, listed or paid for is deleted with everything that belongs to it. This cannot be undone.
  • A bot that has been shared, listed or paid for is removed from your list and kept as a record. Its listings are removed and anyone who paid for access is refunded the unused part from your earnings.

Bots you have already sold to other members stay with them.

Bot list shows every bot you own, running or paused. That includes bots you bought on Bot Market, marked Purchased.

Find a bot

  • Type in Search your bots.
  • Filter by status: Any status, Paused for any reason or one status.
  • Filter by mode: Any mode, Personal or Public.

More bots load as you scroll.

What each status means

  • Running: the bot answers.
  • Paused by you: you paused it.
  • Paused by the Botter Support Team: staff paused it. Contact them through Support.
  • Paused for account closing: your account is closing. Reopening restores it.
  • Paused by your plan: you own more bots than your plan allows.

Actions

Edit, Pause or Unpause, Duplicate and Delete. See Duplicate, pause or delete a bot.

A purchased bot also shows Licence terms and, while they apply, Request a refund and Leave a review. See Bots you bought on Bot Market.

When your plan pauses bots

If you move to a plan with a lower bot limit or your plan ends, the bots over the limit are paused, newest first. Their data is kept.

To choose which bots run, press Keep this bot on a paused bot. It runs again and your newest running bot is paused in its place, so you stay within the limit. Deleting bots or moving to a larger plan also lets paused bots run again.

Every bot has a mode.

  • Personal: only you can use it. It has no share link and no embed, takes no customers and cannot be listed. Every new bot starts Personal.
  • Public: open for sharing, embedding, selling and customers.

A bot can stay Personal for ever. That suits a bot you only use yourself.

Before you make a bot Public

  • Confirm your email address.
  • Accept the latest terms if a banner asks you to.
  • Confirm the bot's declarations in the Mode section. See Declarations.

Make a bot Public

  1. In the Bot builder, open Mode.
  2. Tick the declarations that apply and give any explanation asked for.
  3. Press Confirm declarations.
  4. Press Make Public. It shows Checking while the bot is checked.
  5. When the check passes, the section says This bot is Public.

Changing the mode takes effect now, without Save. If the check takes a while, the section says Still checking. Reload the page later to see the outcome. See The publish check.

Switch back to Personal

Press Switch back to Personal. The bot stops serving its share link, embed and customers at once. A live listing of it is hidden from Bot Market until the bot is Public again.

When Make Public is not offered or is refused

  • A bot you hold on a personal licence stays private. This shows in place of Make Public. A bot bought on Personal use can never be made Public.

If you press Make Public and something stops it, the section says why:

  • Confirm this bot's declarations, beside the Make Public button, before you make it Public. Tick the declarations that apply above it and press Confirm declarations.
  • A refund request is open on this bot: it can be made Public once the Botter Support Team decides the request.
  • Confirm your email address before you make a bot Public: use Send the link again.

A bot you bought

Making a bought bot Public counts as putting it on sale, which ends your right to a refund on its purchase. The builder asks you to confirm first. Confirming the declarations of a bought bot that is already Public, such as one bought by Transfer, does the same. Tick the box above Confirm declarations to go ahead.

Declarations tell the people who use your bot what it does with their information. Your answers show on the bot's Certified by Botterverse page.

A declaration does not stop a bot going Public. It is an honest statement that visitors can judge for themselves. A false declaration breaks the terms.

The seven declarations

  1. Collects personal details: name, email, phone or address.
  2. Handles special category data: health, ethnicity, religion, sexual life or orientation, political opinions, trade union membership, genetic or biometric data.
  3. Handles financial or payment details.
  4. Intended for or likely to be used by under-18s.
  5. Gives advice in a regulated area: medical, legal, financial or insurance.
  6. Makes automated decisions that materially affect a person: eligibility, pricing, screening or scoring.
  7. Sends data to third parties beyond the AI model provider.

Every one except the first has an explanation box under it. The box shows whether or not the declaration is ticked. Fill it in for each one you tick. The box is How the bot does this. For the seventh it is The third parties it sends data to.

Confirm them

  1. In the Bot builder, open Mode.
  2. Tick each declaration that applies and fill in any explanation.
  3. Press Confirm declarations. This takes effect now, without Save.

Declarations the check ticks for you

The publish check reads your bot. If it finds that a declaration applies, it ticks it and locks it. The line under it says Found and locked by our check.

If you disagree, raise a support ticket with the Botter Support Team explaining why it should not apply. Staff can unlock one declaration on one bot. It then says Locked by the Botter Support Team.

Confirming again after a change

Some saved changes to a Public bot mean confirming the declarations again:

  • a change of model
  • a change to an integration
  • a change to the knowledge files
  • a change the check finds a new declaration for

The Mode section then says A change to this bot needs its declarations confirmed again. The bot stays Public meanwhile and its page shows declarations being updated. If you do not confirm them within the time allowed, the bot switches to Personal and you are emailed.

A bot you bought

A bot bought on Bot Market arrives with its declarations cleared. You are now responsible for it, so you confirm your own before it can take new customers.

Before a bot goes Public, Botterverse checks its name, description, instructions and knowledge files. The check runs again on every saved change to a Public bot and when the bot is listed on Bot Market.

What is not allowed

A bot cannot go Public if it is built for:

  • sexual content
  • gambling and betting
  • illegal activity
  • fraud, scams or malicious software
  • harm to children or anyone else
  • hate and harassment
  • impersonating a real person or organisation
  • misleading financial or health claims
  • covert monitoring of people
  • spam, fake reviews or political manipulation
  • passing off work as someone's own for academic credit

The full list is in the terms and conditions.

What you see

While the check runs, the button shows Checking. Then one of these happens:

  • The check passes: the bot is Public.
  • The check refused this bot.: the bot stays Personal. The section names the category that matched and why.
  • Some categories go to staff instead: the bot goes Public and the Botter Support Team looks at it.
  • A declaration applies: it is ticked and locked. If it needs an explanation you have not given, the bot stays Personal until you add it, press Confirm declarations and press Make Public again.
  • The model provider refused this bot's text, so the bot is Personal.: the provider's reason is shown and you are emailed.

After a change to a Public bot

Your change is saved and the check runs again.

  • If it finds a blocked category, the bot switches to Personal and you are emailed.
  • If it finds a category for staff to look at, the bot stays Public.
  • If it finds a new declaration, you confirm the declarations again. See Declarations.

After the bot is live

A small share of conversations is also checked after the fact. A visitor's chat is never interrupted.

Disagree with a result?

Raise a support ticket with the Botter Support Team through Support.

Each Public bot has its own page on your own address, which starts with your username. Share the link anywhere: an email, a social post or your own sales page.

Copy the share link

  1. Make the bot Public. See Personal and Public.
  2. In the Bot builder, open Sharing and embed, under Advanced.
  3. Copy the Share link.

Before the bot is Public the section says The share link and the embed snippet appear once the bot is Public.

Require visitors to sign up

The Require visitors to sign up switch decides whether visitors need an account to chat.

  • On: visitors sign up or sign in first. You know who is chatting and, with the CRM connector, can reach them later.
  • Off: anyone can chat straight away without an account.

A paid bot always needs an account to buy access. Press Save after changing the switch.

Daily credit limit

Every message on a free bot is paid from your credits. A launch can put a lot of people in front of one bot, so each bot has a daily ceiling on what it spends.

  • Leave Daily credit limit empty to use the platform default.
  • Or enter your own limit in whole credits and press Save.

When a bot reaches its limit, free visitors are told it has reached its limit for the day. People who paid for access carry on, as do you. The limit resets at midnight UTC and you are emailed once that day.

Visitor limits

Every visitor can send only so many messages in a minute and in a day. This protects your credits. The limits are the same for every bot. They do not apply to you. People who paid for access are held only to the limit per minute, since their access sets how many messages they have.

When a bot cannot answer

Visitors always see a plain message saying why, such as the bot being paused, busy or at its daily limit.

posts.post_title: Put your bot on your website
posts.post_content:
The embed snippet puts your bot on your own website, where your audience already is.

Steps

  1. Make the bot Public.
  2. In the Bot builder, open Sharing and embed, under Advanced.
  3. Copy the Embed snippet.
  4. Paste it into your website's page, where you want the bot to appear. Most website builders have a box for custom code or HTML.

What visitors see

  • A free bot with Require visitors to sign up off runs inside your page. Visitors chat there with the usual visitor limits.
  • A paid bot or a free bot that needs sign-up shows as a button reading "Chat with" and the bot's name. It opens the bot's own page in a new tab, where the visitor signs in or pays and chats.

Good to know

  • The embed keeps working if you change the bot, since it points at the bot itself.
  • Visitors are told they are talking to an AI assistant before the bot's first reply.
  • The footer carries Report this bot, Certified by Botterverse and, unless your bot style removes it, the powered-by tag.
  • Switching the bot to Personal stops the embed working.

A bot style sets how a bot's own pages look to its customers: the chat page, the paywall, the embed and the sign-up and sign-in pages reached from them. It does not change Botter's Lab. Bot styles are part of Pro Botter and above.

One style can be shared by several of your bots.

Make a style

  1. Open Bot styles in the menu. You can also reach it from Settings, then Branding, then Open Bot styles.
  2. Press New style.
  3. Fill in the cards:
    • Name: the Style name. Only you see it.
    • Branding: drop your logo or choose a file (jpg, png or webp). Add a Display name for the header. Leave it empty to show each bot's own name.
    • Colours: Background, Bot message bubble, Customer message bubble, Text and Accent, used for buttons.
    • Text and corners: the Font, the Chat text size and the Corners.
    • What shows: Show the header, Show the bot's avatar and Show the powered-by tag.
  4. Watch the Preview as you go. Nothing is saved until Save.
  5. Press Save.

If a text and background pair may be hard to read, a warning appears beside it. You can still save, but more contrast helps your customers.

Give a bot its style

  • In the Bot builder, open Style, choose it under Bot style and press Save.
  • Or on Bot styles, press Apply to another bot, choose the Bot and press Apply.

Default style uses the platform's own look.

Change or copy a style

  • Edit changes the style for every bot that uses it. The editor warns you when more than one bot shares it.
  • Duplicate as a new style makes a copy you can change on its own.

The powered-by tag

The tag is a small Botterverse link under the chat, on the paywall and in the embed. It carries your own referral link, so a visitor who clicks it and joins can earn you commission. Pro Botter and above can switch it off.

If your plan changes

Below Pro Botter your bots' pages go back to the default look with the powered-by tag shown. Your styles are kept for when you move back up.

posts.post_title: Certified by Botterverse and Report this bot
posts.post_content:
Every bot's chat page, paywall, embed and Bot Market listing carries two links. Neither can be switched off.

Certified by Botterverse

The link opens the bot's public certification page. It shows:

  • that the bot is genuinely registered on Botterverse
  • the owner's username and how long they have been a member
  • the AI model in use
  • all seven declarations and how each was set: by the owner, by the check or by staff
  • any explanations and third parties
  • when the bot was last screened
  • how long messages are kept, by Botterverse and by the model provider
  • whether the bot is active, paused or suspended

The page certifies where the bot comes from and what its owner declared. It does not certify that the bot is accurate, safe or fit for a purpose.

Report this bot

Anyone can report a bot without an account.

  1. Press Report this bot.
  2. Choose a Reason.
  3. Describe What is wrong.
  4. Add Your email address (optional) if you would like a reply.
  5. Press Send the report.

The Botter Support Team reviews every report.

The paywall charges visitors a one-time price to chat with your bot. It is part of Novice Botter and above.

A purchase is called an access. It can include a set number of messages, with top-ups for more. There is no subscription: buyers pay once.

Switch it on

  1. Make the bot Public. See Personal and Public.
  2. In the Bot builder, open Paywall and pricing.
  3. Switch on Sell access to this bot.
  4. Fill in the One-time price and, if you like, a Message cap and a top-up. See Prices, message caps and top-ups.
  5. Choose a Money-back guarantee. See The guarantee and refunds.
  6. Press Save.

What buyers see

Your bot's page shows the paywall in place of the chat:

  • the bot's name, its rating if you show it, its description and its starters under Things you can ask it
  • the price, the messages it buys and any top-up
  • the guarantee, in fixed wording

A buyer needs an account, so a signed-out visitor is asked to Sign up or Sign in first. The buyer ticks a box to agree that access starts as soon as they open the bot and that a refund is only given under your guarantee. They then press Pay followed by the price, such as "Pay $29.00". They pay through our checkout.

Once they have paid, the page opens the chat. Their purchase appears on their Bots I bought page.

Where the money goes

Each sale is added to your earnings, less the platform fee for your plan. See Your sales.

Ratings

People who paid for access can rate your bot from 1 to 5 stars once they have sent a few messages. Switch Show the bot's rating on its paywall page on or off and press Save.

Who cannot buy

Nobody in the EU can pay. Visitors there are told paid features are not available in their country.

If your plan changes

Below Novice Botter the paywall closes to new buyers. Existing buyers keep their access.

Every message your buyers send is paid from your credits. A message cap protects you from a buyer who pays once and chats for ever.

The fields

In the Bot builder, open Paywall and pricing.

  • One-time price: what a buyer pays, in US dollars, such as 29.00.
  • Message cap: how many messages the price includes. Leave it empty for no cap.
  • Top-up size in messages and Top-up price: a pack of extra messages a buyer can buy when they reach the cap.

Press Save to keep them.

Rules Save checks

  • The price and the top-up price each have a minimum. Save tells you the minimum if yours is lower.
  • A top-up needs both a size and a price. Fill in both or leave both empty.
  • A top-up needs a message cap, since a buyer with no cap never reaches one.

A price saved before a minimum was raised keeps selling until you next change it.

What buyers see when the cap is reached

The chat tells them their messages have run out and offers Top up. On Bots I bought their access shows the messages left and a button such as "Top up 50 messages for $9.00".

If you offer no top-up, a buyer whose messages run out can buy a fresh access at the paywall.

Fees

The platform fee is taken from each access and each top-up, as for any sale. See Your sales.

Changing the price later

A change applies to new buyers. Earlier buyers keep what they bought.

Choose a guarantee

In Paywall and pricing, choose a Money-back guarantee: No guarantee, 7 days or 14 days. Only the periods within the platform's refund period are offered, so you may see fewer. Press Save.

The paywall shows the guarantee in fixed wording, so every buyer reads the same promise. Changing it later does not change what earlier buyers were promised.

Earnings are released after a holdback. A longer guarantee promised anywhere else, such as on your own sales page, may leave you unable to refund from your earnings.

How a buyer claims

  1. The buyer opens Bots I bought.
  2. While the guarantee lasts, they press Request a refund.
  3. They answer Why are you asking for a refund? and press Send the claim.

A claim is made on the original purchase, never on a top-up by itself.

What you do with a claim

You are emailed and the sale on your Sales page shows the claim and its reason. It says when it will be refunded automatically. Before then you can:

  • press Refund to refund it now
  • press Ask the Botter Support Team to review, for example if you suspect abuse. Staff then decide it.

If you do neither by the date shown, the claim is refunded automatically. A guarantee refund takes the full price from your earnings, even where they go below zero. It also ends the access, so unused top-ups on it are refunded too.

Refunds outside a guarantee

Nothing forces you to refund outside a guarantee. You can still refund an access or a top-up from Sales within the refund period. See Refunds and disputes.

When a bot is taken away

If you delete a bot that people paid for or your account closes, everyone with unused messages is refunded the unused part from your earnings.

posts.post_title: Browse and buy on Bot Market
posts.post_content:
Bot Market is where members sell bots to each other. Buying a bot here gives you the bot itself, to run on your own credits. Every plan can buy.

Find a bot

  1. Open Browse in the menu.
  2. Type in Search Bot Market or use the filters: Any category, Any model, Any sale type, Any owner, Any release date, Includes integrations and 4 stars and up.
  3. Sort by Relevance, Top rated, Price high to low or Price low to high.

Each card shows the bot's name, rating, price, description, category and model. You might also like suggests more at the foot.

Read the listing

Press a card to open the listing. It shows:

  • the sale type, the licence and the price
  • the description and the reviews, each marked Verified purchase
  • About the seller: their rating, verified sales, member since date and badges
  • verified sales, conversations and revenue, where the seller shows them
  • Customers who also bought, You might also like and More from this seller

See Transfer, Multi-sell and licences before you buy.

Buy

  1. Press Buy. The Checkout page opens.
  2. Read The licence you are buying: the licence summary and The seller's licence terms.
  3. Tick the box that says the bot is delivered as soon as you pay, that a refund is only given if it does not work or is not as described, that putting it on sale ends any right to a refund and that an approved refund is less a processing fee.
  4. Tick I accept the seller's licence terms shown above.
  5. Press Pay followed by the price, such as "Pay $19.00". Then pay through our checkout.

You return to Confirming your payment. Once confirmed, the bot is in your Bot list marked Purchased and you are emailed.

If you leave the checkout before paying, Checkout cancelled confirms nothing was charged.

When you cannot buy

  • You cannot buy your own listing.
  • You are at your plan's bot limit, so you cannot add another bot. A bought bot counts towards your limit.
  • Purchases are not available in your country. Nobody in the EU can pay.
  • This listing is not available. The listing is no longer on sale.

If a listing changes while you are paying, so it can no longer be delivered, your payment is refunded in full and you are told.

Next

Bots you bought on Bot Market

The two sale types

  • Transfer: ownership moves to the buyer. The seller no longer has the bot and cannot sell it again. It sells once.
  • Multi-sell: each buyer receives their own copy carrying the listing's licence. The seller keeps the original and can keep selling it.

A buyer keeps the version they bought. A later update by the seller does not reach earlier buyers.

The four licences

  • Personal use: you may use the bot yourself. You may not make it Public, put it behind a paywall, list it for sale or edit and rebrand it.
  • Resell rights: you may use the bot, make it Public and put it behind a paywall. You may sell copies of it on Personal use by Multi-sell. You may not edit or rebrand it.
  • Master resell rights: as Resell rights, but you may sell copies on Personal use or Resell rights by Multi-sell.
  • PLR: you may use the bot, make it Public, put it behind a paywall and edit and rebrand it. You may sell it by Multi-sell or Transfer on Personal use, Resell rights or Master resell rights.

A bot you built yourself carries no licence. You can list it on any of the four.

Who grants the licence

Botterverse sells the bot as seller of record. The licence to use it is granted by the seller under their own licence terms, which you accept at checkout. Read a seller's terms on their licence terms page.

Transfer of a Public bot

A bot that was Public stays Public for its existing customers, who now use the buyer's credits. It moves to the buyer's address and its old address forwards to the new one. Embeds keep working. Running A/B tests stop. The buyer confirms their own declarations before it takes new customers.

What never moves with a bot

Integration passwords and keys. A bought bot arrives with its integrations switched off. Enter your own credentials and switch each one on.

Bots I bought lists other members' bots you have bought paid access to through their paywall. You chat with these bots but do not own them.

Bots you own, including bots bought on Bot Market, are in your Bot list instead. See Bots you bought on Bot Market.

What each entry shows

  • The bot's name, which opens its page.
  • The messages you have left. An access with no cap shows Unlimited messages.
  • Open chat.
  • A top-up button, such as "Top up 50 messages for $9.00", when the seller offers one.
  • Money-back guarantee until a date, while the seller's guarantee lasts.

Top up

  1. Press the top-up button.
  2. Pay through our checkout.
  3. You return to the chat with the extra messages added.

Claim the guarantee

  1. Press Request a refund while the guarantee lasts.
  2. Answer Why are you asking for a refund?
  3. Press Send the claim.

The seller is told. You are emailed when the claim is decided. If the seller neither refunds it nor asks staff to review it by their deadline, it is refunded automatically.

Rate a bot

In the chat, once you have sent a few messages, Rate this bot lets you give 1 to 5 stars. You can change your rating later.

posts.post_title: Bots you bought on Bot Market
posts.post_content:
A bot bought on Bot Market is yours. It sits in your Bot list marked Purchased and runs on your own credits.

What you can do with it

That depends on its licence. See Transfer, Multi-sell and licences.

  • On Personal use, Resell rights or Master resell rights, the instructions and knowledge files are hidden. You can still choose the model, set up integrations, give it a style and, where the licence allows, make it Public and paywall it.
  • On PLR you can edit and rebrand it. To list it for sale you must rename it first. The new name must differ from the name it arrived with.

Before you use it with customers

  • Integrations arrive switched off with no credentials. Enter your own and switch each one on.
  • Declarations arrive cleared. Confirm your own in the Mode section before it takes new customers.

Actions in the Bot list

  • Licence terms: the seller's current terms.
  • Request a refund: while the refund window lasts and you have not put the bot on sale.
  • Leave a review: one review per purchase.

Request a refund

Bot Market refunds are decided by the Botter Support Team and given only when the bot does not work or is not as described.

  1. Press Request a refund.
  2. Answer Why are you asking for a refund?
  3. Press Send the request.

If staff approve it, the refund is the price you paid less a processing fee. You are emailed with the decision.

While a request is open you cannot make the bot Public, switch on its paywall or list it.

Putting it on sale ends the right to a refund

Making the bot Public, switching on its paywall or listing it shows you are happy with it. So does confirming the declarations of a bought bot that is already Public, such as one bought by Transfer. After that, Request a refund is no longer offered. The app asks you to confirm first. For the declarations it is a tick box above Confirm declarations.

Leave a review

  1. Press Leave a review.
  2. Choose Your rating, from 1 to 5 stars.
  3. Write Your review (optional).
  4. Press Publish the review.

The review shows on the listing and the seller's profile at once, marked Verified purchase. The seller may post one public reply.

Duplicating and exporting

A bought bot cannot be duplicated until its refund window has passed or you have put it on sale. For the same reason the data export leaves out its instructions, starters and knowledge files until then.

Selling on Bot Market is part of Pro Botter and above. Only a Public bot you own can be listed. Each bot has one listing at a time.

Before you start

  • The bot is Public with its declarations confirmed.
  • The bot has a category.
  • Your licence terms are saved in Settings. See Your licence terms.
  • Your email address is confirmed.

Steps

  1. Open My listings in the menu.
  2. Under List a bot for sale, press List it beside the bot.
  3. In Listing details, write the Description and add Tags, separated with commas. Or press Suggest a description and tags, which uses no credits.
  4. In Sale type and licence, choose Transfer or Multi-sell and the Licence. Only the licences this bot's own licence can pass on are offered.
  5. In Price, enter the Price (USD). The minimum shows under the field. Add an Affiliate share (%) if you want other members to promote it. See Promote a listing.
  6. Check the line You receive to see what each sale pays you after the platform fee and any affiliate share. The category averages beside it help you price.
  7. In On the listing, choose what shows:
    • Show verified sales and conversations
    • Show verified revenue
    • Show in Bot Market: switch it off to sell only through the listing's own page.
    • Require attribution on copies
  8. Press Submit. Or press Save as draft to finish later.

The listing shows In review while it is checked, then Live. If the check flags something, it stays in review until the Botter Support Team clears it. You are emailed when it goes live.

The listing's name

The name is set for you. It is the bot's name. A bot you hold on Resell rights or Master resell rights is listed as its name followed by "by" and your username.

Your listing's own page

Every listing has a page you can share with your own list or on social media. Press View on a live listing in My listings to open it and copy its address.

Change a live listing

Press Edit, make your changes and press Save. The change is live at once while the listing is checked again in the background. If the check flags it, the listing goes back to In review.

A listing in review shows Open in place of Edit. You can look at it but not change it until it is decided.

Take a listing off sale

  1. In My listings, press Edit on the live listing.
  2. Press Unlist, beside Save.
  3. Press Unlist again to confirm. Keep it on sale stops. The listing goes back to Draft and cannot be bought until you submit it again.

Listing statuses

  • Draft: saved but not on sale.
  • In review: being checked or waiting for the Botter Support Team.
  • Live: on sale.
  • Sold: a Transfer that has sold.
  • Removed: taken down by staff or removed with the bot.
  • Hidden while closing: your account is closing.

If a listing will not submit, see When a listing is blocked.

When something stops a listing being submitted, the form says why at the top and again under Submit is not available yet. Most reasons have a link beside them to where you fix it.

Reasons and fixes

  • Add your licence terms in Settings before listing a bot. Press Open Settings, fill in Licence terms and press Save. See Your licence terms.
  • Confirm this bot's declarations before listing it. Press Confirm them in the Bot builder's Mode section and press Confirm declarations.
  • Choose a category for this bot in the Bot builder before listing it. This one shows under the Category field in Listing details, not in the list at the top. Press Change it in the Bot builder beside the field, choose a category and press Save.
  • This bot's name still matches the name it arrived with or the name of an earlier bot in its line. A PLR bot must be renamed. Press Open the Bot builder, give it a new name in Details and press Save.
  • Accept the updated terms before listing a bot. Press Accept the updated terms and accept them in the banner.
  • Confirm your email address before you submit a listing. Press Send the link again and open the link in the email.
  • This bot has an open refund request. It can be listed once the Botter Support Team decides the request.
  • Only a Public bot you own whose licence lets you sell it can be listed. Make the bot Public. A bot held on Personal use cannot be listed.
  • This bot already has a listing. Change that listing in My listings rather than adding a second.
  • Selling on Bot Market is not part of your plan. Selling needs Pro Botter or above.

A listing stuck in review

In review means the check flagged something for the Botter Support Team. You cannot change the listing until it is decided. It goes live once staff clear it. If staff uphold the flag, the listing is removed and you are emailed why.

A live listing missing from Bot Market

A listing that shows Live in My listings can still be hidden from buyers:

  • the bot is Personal or paused
  • your plan is below Pro Botter
  • your account is suspended
  • staff rejected your licence terms, until you save new terms that pass the check

It shows again as soon as the cause is put right. A hidden listing's page says it is unavailable and cannot be bought.

Buyers of your Bot Market listings accept your licence terms when they buy. You need saved terms before you can list a bot. The Licence terms section of Settings is part of Pro Botter and above.

Botterverse does not provide legal advice. These terms are yours and you are responsible for making them legally compliant.

Write your terms

  1. Open Settings and then Licence terms.
  2. Press Copy our template to start from Botterverse's template, then adapt it. Or write your own in Your licence terms.
  3. Press Save.

Copying the template is a one-off. A later change to the template does not change your copy.

Where buyers read them

  • On the checkout page, under the platform's summary of the licence.
  • On your licence terms page, which anyone can read.
  • From Licence terms beside the bot in their Bot list.

Tell your buyers about a change

Saving sends no email. To tell your buyers, press Notify my buyers. Each buyer who still holds a licence is emailed a link to your terms page, never the wording itself. The button is offered once each time you save new terms.

Checks on your terms

Saved terms are checked like a listing, since buyers read them. Terms that fail the check are still saved and the Botter Support Team looks at them. If staff reject them, your listings are hidden from Bot Market until you save new terms that pass.

While you have a live listing, the terms cannot be emptied.

posts.post_title: Your seller profile, reviews and badges
posts.post_content:
Every member has a public seller profile on Bot Market. Open yours from My profile in the menu.

What it shows

  • Your username, avatar and Member since date.
  • Your badges.
  • Average rating across your Bot Market reviews.
  • Verified sales: completed Bot Market sales paid through Botterverse that were not refunded or disputed.
  • Access rating: the rating from people who paid for access to your bots, kept apart from Bot Market reviews.
  • Live listings and Reviews.

Your avatar is set in Settings, under Account.

Badges

Badges are earned and show only while their condition holds:

  • Founder: your subscription uses the founders coupon.
  • Verified Seller: you have been paid out or your payouts are set up.
  • 10 Sales: ten verified sales.
  • Top Rated: a high average rating from enough reviews.

Reply to a review

  1. Open Sales.
  2. Find the sale with the review and press Reply.
  3. Write Your public reply and press Post the reply.

You can post one reply to each review and change it later with Edit the reply. Reviews and replies are checked automatically. A flagged one stays up unless the Botter Support Team decides to hide it.

Sales lists every paywall access, message top-up and Bot Market sale of your bots, newest first. More load as you scroll.

What each sale shows

  • The bot and the type: Paywall access, Message top-up or Bot Market sale.
  • The buyer's username and the date.
  • Price: what the buyer paid.
  • Platform fee: Botterverse's fee for your plan. It is a percentage plus a fixed amount per sale, never more than the sale.
  • Your share: what is added to your earnings.
  • Status: Paid, Partly refunded, Refunded, Disputed or Pending.

Actions on a sale

  • Refund: for a paywall access or top-up within the refund period. See Refunds and disputes.
  • Ask the Botter Support Team to review: on an open guarantee claim. See The guarantee and refunds.
  • Comment: on an open Bot Market refund request.
  • Report a licence breach: on a Bot Market sale.
  • Reply: on a sale with a review. See Your seller profile, reviews and badges.

Where your share goes

Your share is added to your earnings. It can be withdrawn once the holdback has passed. See Earnings, holds and refunds.

Sale emails

To be emailed for each sale, review and commission, switch on Sales in Settings under Email notifications.

Your earnings are what Botterverse owes you from your sales and affiliate commissions. Botterverse takes every payment as seller of record and pays you your share when you withdraw.

Open Payouts to see them under Your earnings.

Available to withdraw

The amount you can withdraw now.

Held for refunds

Earnings from a sale wait for a holdback before they can be withdrawn, so a refund in that time can come straight from them. Each held amount shows:

  • Withdrawable from a date, with the bot and the sale it came from
  • Held until its dispute or refund request closes, where a buyer has disputed a payment or asked for a refund.

Commission on a promoted listing waits in the same way. Subscription commissions are only added once their refund period has passed, so they are withdrawable at once.

Customer hold

If one of your bots that people paid for stops serving them, such as when it is paused, an amount is held for those customers in case they are refunded. The page names the bots. It is released as soon as those bots serve their customers again.

Refunds after you have withdrawn

A refund that arrives after you have withdrawn can take your earnings below zero. It is recovered from your future earnings and you cannot withdraw until they are back above zero. Money already paid into your bank is never taken back.

Refund a paywall sale

Outside a guarantee, refunding is your choice. You can refund a paywall access or a message top-up from Sales within the refund period.

  1. Press Refund on the sale.
  2. Check the breakdown: Refunded to the buyer and Covered by your earnings.
  3. Press Confirm the refund.

The buyer's payment is refunded and the full price comes from your earnings. Botterverse keeps its fee, since the refund is your decision.

  • Refunding an access ends it, along with any unused top-ups on it.
  • Refunding a top-up only removes the extra messages it bought. The access carries on.

When your earnings do not cover it

The breakdown adds a Shortfall and a Card processing fee. Press the button that reads Pay followed by the amount and by card. Once you have paid the shortfall, the refund goes ahead. Only the shortfall is added to your earnings. If you do not pay, nothing is refunded.

Bot Market refunds

You cannot refund a Bot Market sale yourself. The buyer asks the Botter Support Team, who refund only when the bot does not work or is not as described.

When a request is open, the sale shows Refund request and its reason. Press Comment to give your side before the date shown, then Save the comment. While it is open, your share of that sale cannot be withdrawn.

An approved refund returns the price less a processing fee. A Transfer bot comes back to you exactly as it was at the sale. A Multi-sell buyer loses their copy and your original is untouched.

Disputes

If a buyer disputes a payment with their bank, the sale shows Disputed with the note The buyer's bank is deciding a dispute on this sale, so it cannot be refunded here. Your share is held until the bank decides. You are emailed.

A lost dispute is treated as a refund. The dispute fees Stripe keeps come from your earnings when the dispute closes, won or lost.

Report a licence breach

If a Bot Market buyer uses a bot outside its licence:

  1. Press Report a licence breach on the sale.
  2. Describe What has the buyer done outside the licence?
  3. Add Evidence, as text and links.
  4. Press Send the report.

The Botter Support Team decides it. An upheld breach revokes the buyer's licence and removes the bot without a refund to them.

You can build, list and sell with no payout account at all. Your earnings build up until you are ready. Payouts are made by Stripe into your own bank account. You enter your bank details on Stripe's own form, so Botterverse never sees them.

When you can set up

Payout set-up on the Payouts page says You can set up payouts once you have the minimum withdrawal to withdraw. Once you reach it, the card says You have enough to withdraw. Set up payouts to receive it.

Steps

  1. Open Payouts.
  2. Choose Your country, the country where you live, if asked.
  3. Press Set up payouts.
  4. Enter your bank details on Stripe's form.
  5. When you return, the card says Payouts are set up.

If you leave the form part way, press Continue on Stripe's form to finish.

Other messages you may see

  • The Botter Support Team is setting up your payouts and will email you once it is done. Some payouts are set up by hand. You are emailed when it is done.
  • Stripe can no longer pay your bank account. Update your bank details to withdraw again. Press Update your bank details.
  • Stripe cannot yet pay out to the country on your account. Nothing is blocked and your earnings still build up. Payouts go by the country of the bank account you enter.

Change your bank details

Press Update your bank details on the Payout set-up card.

Next

Withdraw your earnings

Once payouts are set up, the Withdraw card appears on Payouts. Its heading line says the smallest withdrawal.

Steps

  1. Enter the Amount in US dollars.
  2. Press Show the fees.
  3. Check the figures: Withdrawal, Stripe's payout fees, the Exchange rate if your bank uses another currency and What will arrive.
  4. Press Confirm the withdrawal. To start again, press Change the amount.

Stripe's payout fees are passed on at cost. If more is charged than Stripe keeps, the difference comes back to your earnings.

Track a withdrawal

Withdrawals lists each one with its date, fees and status:

  • Requested: waiting to be sent. Some are sent on set days, shown as sending on a date.
  • Being sent by the Botter Support Team or Being processed by the Botter Support Team: staff are sending it by hand.
  • Sent: on its way to your bank. You are emailed.
  • Paid into your bank account.
  • Failed. Check your bank details or Returned by your bank. Check your bank details: the amount is back in your earnings.
  • Cancelled.

Cancel a withdrawal

While it shows Requested, press Cancel and then Cancel the withdrawal. Its amount and fee come back to your earnings. Once it is being sent it cannot be cancelled.

Credits pay for every message your bots send. Each message uses credits by its real size, so a short answer costs less than a long one. A more expensive AI model uses more credits than a cheaper one.

You pay for:

  • the chats visitors and customers have with your bots
  • your own testing in the preview
  • conversation insights, if you switch them on

Uploading knowledge files, the importer, category suggestions and listing suggestions use no credits.

Where credits come from

  • Plan credits: your plan adds included credits each month. On an annual plan they still arrive monthly. Unused plan credits expire at the next renewal or plan change.
  • Credit packs: bought on Billing and credits. See Buy a credit pack.
  • Auto top-up: buys credits for you when they run low. See Auto top-up.
  • Promo codes: add bonus credits. See Redeem a promo code.

Credits you buy never expire.

See your credits

  • The credits pill at the top of every page shows your balance.
  • Billing and credits, under Credits and usage, shows Credits left, the graph Credits used over time and the history of every change to your balance.

The history labels each change, such as Messages, Plan credits, Credits bought, Promo code, Added by the Botter Support Team, Refunded purchase or Adjustment.

When credits run low

You are emailed when your credits fall below your auto top-up threshold. When your credits cannot cover a message, your bots stop answering everyone, including people who paid for access. You are emailed again. Top up to start them again. See Top up your credits.

One message often costs a small part of a credit. The app keeps your credits exactly, to four decimal places.

  • Your balance shows whole credits, rounded down, wherever it appears: the credits pill, the Dashboard and Credits left on Billing and credits. Rounding down means it never shows more than you have.
  • The history on Billing and credits shows each change to four decimal places, such as -0.0064 for one message.

So a balance of 11,999.7 credits shows as 11,999 credits. The part credit is still yours and is used by your next messages.

A credit pack is a set number of credits bought in one payment. Bigger packs include bonus credits on top.

Steps

  1. Open Billing and credits.
  2. Open Buy credits. Each pack shows its name, its credits and its price. A pack with a bonus reads, for example, "5,500 credits, including 500 bonus credits".
  3. Press Buy beside the pack. Our checkout opens in a new tab.
  4. Pay. The credits are added to your balance as soon as the payment goes through.

Bought credits never expire.

Good to know

  • Buy with the email address on your account, so the payment is matched to it.
  • Nobody in the EU can pay for credits.
  • If no packs are on sale, the section says so and points you to auto top-up instead.
  • If a pack's payment is refunded, its credits are removed, up to your balance at the time.

Auto top-up buys credits for you when your balance runs low, so a busy launch never leaves your bots silent. It is off until you switch it on.

Switch it on

  1. Open Billing and credits and then Auto top-up.
  2. Read the short statement. It says when auto top-up charges, how the amount is set and how to switch it off. The full detail is under Read how auto top-up works in full in our terms and conditions.
  3. Press Agree and switch on. Switching on is your agreement to the charges.

Choose when and how much

  1. Enter Top up when my credits fall below, in whole credits.
  2. Enter the Top-up amount in dollars. The line below shows how many credits it buys, one credit for each cent.
  3. Press Save.

How it charges

  • It charges the card on your plan's subscription. It is only available once you have an active plan with a card on file.
  • You are emailed each time it charges.
  • Only a set number of top-ups can be charged in one day. After that it pauses until the next day and you are emailed.
  • Auto top-up buys credits at one credit a cent, with no pack bonus.

When a charge does not go through

  • Your bank asks you to approve it: the top-up is not retried, since only you can approve it. Buy a credit pack instead.
  • The card is declined: it is tried once more later. If that fails too, auto top-up switches off and you are emailed.

When it switches off

  • When you press Switch off.
  • When your plan ends.
  • When you close your account. Reopening leaves it off until you switch it on again.

If we update the auto top-up statement, auto top-up pauses until you agree to the new one. You are emailed when this happens.

A promo code adds bonus credits to your balance. It never changes a price.

Steps

  1. Open Billing and credits and then Promo code.
  2. Type the code in Promo code.
  3. Press Redeem.

The credits show in your history as Promo code.

If you try too many codes in a short time, you are asked to wait before trying again.

A discount on a plan is a different thing: it is a coupon you enter at the cart checkout when you buy the plan.

You can move up or down between plans and between monthly and yearly billing.

Steps

  1. Open Billing and credits and then Your plan.
  2. Under Change your plan, press Change plan. The upgrade checkout opens in a new tab.
  3. Choose the new plan and pay the prorated amount.

Any page your plan does not include also has a Change plan button.

What a change costs

  • Monthly billing: moving to a cheaper plan part way through the month loses the unused part of it. Moving just before your plan renews loses nothing.
  • Yearly billing: moving to monthly billing or to a cheaper yearly plan refunds each whole unused month after the current one. The rest of the current month is not refunded.

What happens to your credits

The first payment on the new plan replaces your old plan's unused included credits with the new plan's. Credits you bought stay.

Moving to a smaller plan

  • Bots over the new bot limit are paused, newest first. Use Keep this bot to choose which run. See Your Bot list.
  • Below Pro Botter your listings are hidden and your bots' pages go back to the default style.
  • Below Novice Botter paywalls close to new buyers.
  • Moving to Apprentice Botter takes you out of the affiliate programme. Commission already earned is unaffected.
  • A/B tests stop below Master Botter.

Moving back up restores them.

Only one plan at a time

You hold one plan at a time. The checkout refuses a second plan, so always change through Change plan.

If plan changes are not available

Plan changes are not available here yet. means the upgrade checkout is not set up. Contact the Botter Support Team.

Cancelling takes one press and you keep your plan to the end of the period you paid for.

Steps

  1. Open Billing and credits and then Your plan.
  2. Press Cancel my plan.
  3. Read what happens, then press Cancel my plan again to confirm. Press Go back to keep it.

Monthly plans

You keep your plan until the end of the period you have paid for. Nothing more is charged. After that your account carries on without a plan.

Yearly plans

Your plan ends at the end of the current month of your year. Each whole month left after it is refunded to the card you paid with. The confirmation shows the months and the amount before you confirm.

Changed your mind?

Until the plan ends, Your plan shows Ends and a date, with a Keep my plan button. Press it and your plan carries on and renews as before.

After your plan ends

  • Your account stays open. You can still sign in and chat on bots you bought access to.
  • Your bots are paused until you choose a plan again. Their data is kept.
  • Unused plan credits expire. Credits you bought stay.
  • Auto top-up switches off.

To close your account completely, see Close your account.

Plans and credit packs are sold through our cart software and payment processor. They send your receipts and invoices and keep your saved card.

Find an invoice or change a card

  1. Open Billing and credits and then Your plan.
  2. Under Invoices, receipts and saved cards, press Open the customer area.
  3. Sign in to the customer area with your billing login. It is separate from your Botter's Lab account.

Your billing login

Buying a plan makes a billing login on the Botterverse website for the email address you bought with.

  • Set its password from the link in the email you receive after the purchase. The link works once and expires after 24 hours.
  • Sign in with your username or email address and that password.
  • Forgotten the password? Link expired? On the billing sign-in page choose Forgotten password?, enter your username or email address and press Send me a link. We email you a link to choose a new password.

If you already had a help desk sign-in under that email address, no billing login is made and no such email is sent. Sign in to the customer area with your help desk sign-in.

The email your receipts go to

Receipts and invoices go to the email on your Botter's Lab account. To change it, change your email in Settings. The change reaches your billing account and your billing login too. See Change your email or password.

Bot purchases

Bot access, message top-ups and Bot Market purchases are single payments. Each one sends its own receipt and no card is saved.

Analytics shows how one bot is used. Open it from the menu, from a bot on the Dashboard or from Full analytics in the Bot builder's Analytics section.

Choose the bot under Bot and the period with Date range.

Every figure has an info mark beside it. Tap or hover over it for a short explanation.

What each plan shows

Basic: Novice Botter and above

  • Conversations, with the change against the previous period of the same length.
  • Messages, with messages per conversation.
  • Credits used, with credits per message.
  • Revenue: your share of the bot's sales, with the number of access purchases.
  • Conversations over time: a graph of conversations started.

Deeper: Expert Botter and above

  • Category benchmarks: the category average for messages per buyer, price and conversion beside This bot. A benchmark is hidden until enough bots in the category feed it.
  • Busiest hours: visitor messages by hour of the day, in your own timezone.
  • Top conversation starters: how often each starter opened a conversation and its share of openings.

Advanced: Master Botter

  • Conversion: Paywall views, Listing views, Purchases and Conversion, which is purchases over views.

On Apprentice Botter the page shows no panels, apart from conversation insights if you switch them on.

Conversation insights

If insights are switched on for the bot, the Conversation insights panel shows here too. See Conversation insights.

A bot you bought

Figures start from the day the bot became yours.

Insights read the conversations your bot had with the public at regular intervals. They tell you what visitors asked that it could not answer, what they came for and what you could add to its instructions or knowledge.

Insights are off until you switch them on. No plan includes them, so each run is paid from your credits.

Switch them on

  1. In the Bot builder, open Analytics, under Advanced.
  2. Read how often a run happens and what a run typically costs at your plan's rate.
  3. Switch on Conversation insights.
  4. Press Save.

Read the results

Open Analytics and choose the bot. The Conversation insights panel shows the latest run:

  • Unanswered questions: what visitors asked that the bot could not answer, with how many conversations asked it.
  • Common topics: what visitors came for.
  • Suggested additions: changes to the instructions or knowledge. Each says where it goes. Press Add to knowledge or Add to instructions beside one to add it.

To be emailed when a new report is ready, switch on Insights in Settings under Email notifications.

A run that was skipped

The panel says why, for example that your credit balance was too low. Nothing is charged for a skipped or failed run.

When insights are not offered

Insights are not offered on a bot whose instructions you cannot see, such as one bought on Resell rights. A bot you buy arrives with insights switched off.

An A/B test shows visitors different versions of a bot's instructions and starters, then tells you which one works better. A/B tests are part of Master Botter.

The bot as it is now is the control. Each variant has its own instructions and starters. Price is never tested.

Set up a test

  1. Open A/B tests in the menu and choose the Bot.
  2. Under Set-up, enter the Control's share (%) of new conversations.
  3. For each variant, enter a Variant name, its Share (%), its Instructions and its Starters, one to a line.
  4. Press Add a variant for more. The shares must add up to 100%.
  5. Press Save. The test is kept as a Draft.
  6. Press Start the test.

Each variant is checked like a bot going Public before the test starts. The button shows Checking meanwhile. A variant that needs a declaration you have not confirmed stops the start: confirm it in the bot's Mode section and start again.

While it runs

The status shows Running. The shares and variants can no longer change. The same visitor always sees the same version.

Results shows each variant against the control over the whole test:

  • Conversations
  • Messages per conversation
  • Returning customers
  • Paywall conversion
  • Revenue per conversation

Under each one a line says how it compares, such as There is not enough data yet to compare this variant with the control. or that it converts better than the control with a given confidence.

Finish a test

  • Choose as winner: the variant's instructions and starters become the bot's own and the test stops.
  • Keep the control: the bot stays as it is and the test stops.
  • Stop the test: stops without changing the bot.

Then press Start a new test to try something else.

When a test stops by itself

A test stops if the bot is sold by Transfer, deleted or your plan drops below Master Botter. Pausing the bot or switching it to Personal leaves it running.

When a test is not available

A test is not available for this bot, since you cannot see and edit its instructions. This applies to bots bought on Personal use, Resell rights or Master resell rights.

The importer builds a bot from a setup you already have somewhere else, such as a custom GPT. You paste the content in. It does not connect to your account anywhere else.

The importer uses no credits. Nothing is saved until the last step.

Steps

  1. Open Import a bot in the menu.
  2. Instructions: paste your existing instructions and press Continue.
  3. Files: press Browse to add knowledge files, then Continue. The limits are shown above the button.
  4. Integrations: add any services the bot should call, using the same form as the Bot builder. Press Add integration for each one. This step is optional. Press Continue.
  5. Review: the importer suggests a Name, Description, Category and Starters, one to a line from your instructions. Your Instructions show below them. Check each field and change anything you like. Anything that could not be carried across is listed under Not carried across. Press Continue.
  6. Create bot: check the summary and press Create bot.

The new bot opens in the Bot builder as Personal. Test it in Preview, then make it Public when you are ready.

If something goes wrong

  • If the instructions cannot be read automatically, they are kept as you pasted them. Check each field yourself on the review step.
  • If no suggestions can be made, fill in the name, description and category yourself.
  • At your plan's bot limit, the first step and the last step say so. Free a place or change your plan.
  • Integrations are not part of Apprentice Botter. You can carry on without one.

The affiliate programme pays you commission on the plans of the members you refer and on the Bot Market listings you promote. It is part of Novice Botter and above.

Join

  1. Open Affiliates at the foot of the menu.
  2. Press Join the affiliate programme.
  3. Your link appears under Your link. Copy it and share it.

Joining is open to active accounts only. If joining fails because your account could not be found on the Botterverse website, contact the Botter Support Team.

What earns commission

  • Subscription payments by members who joined through your link: their first payment and every renewal.
  • Bot Market sales through your listing links, at the share the seller set. See Promote a listing.

Nothing else earns commission. Credit packs earn none.

Rules

  • Referring yourself breaks the terms, whether through your own account, another account of yours or your own card. It is checked. A repeat offender is banned and their earnings forfeited.
  • Commission is single level. You earn on the members you refer, not on the members they refer.

If your plan changes

Moving down to Apprentice Botter takes you out of the programme and your link stops earning. So does your plan ending. Commission already earned is unaffected. Moving back up to Novice Botter or above puts you back in.

Next

  • Your referral link
  • Commissions and when they are paid
