  • Refer people and earn commission

Your referral link ends in your own username. Anyone who clicks it is taken to the Botterverse website with your referral attached. If they then buy a plan, they are recorded as your referral.

Where to find it

Open Affiliates. Your link is under Your link, with a button to copy it.

Where to share it

  • Your email list and social posts.
  • Your own website or sales page.
  • Your bots: the powered-by tag on your bots' pages already carries your link, so a customer who clicks it and joins counts as yours. See Bot styles.

Track your referrals

Referrals lists each referral with its date and status, with a count for each status. Use the Date range control to choose a period.

The referrals are read from the affiliate programme on the Botterverse website. If it is not answering, the page shows the last figures it read and says so.

Good to know

  • You only ever see your own username in the link.
  • Buyers should use the email address they sign up with, so their plan is matched to their account.

You can promote another member's Bot Market listing and earn a share of each sale made through your link. You need the affiliate programme on your plan: Novice Botter and above.

Copy your listing link

  1. Open the listing on Bot Market.
  2. Press Promote.
  3. Copy your listing link.

A sale made within the affiliate period of a click on your link earns you the listing's affiliate share. If several members' links were clicked, the last click counts.

What you earn

The seller sets the share as a percentage. It is taken from what is left of the price after the platform fee.

Track it

Promoted listings on Affiliates lists each listing sold through your links, with Sales and Commission earned, net of anything taken back by a refund. Each one shows its link again.

As a seller

To let other members promote your listing, enter an Affiliate share (%) when you list it. See List a bot for sale.

posts.post_title: Commissions and when they are paid
posts.post_content:
How much you earn

  • A referred member's first ever payment earns you a larger share.
  • Every later payment earns a smaller share. That includes renewals and the first payment after the member changes plan.

The rates are set by Botterverse and can change. The Botter Support Team can tell you the current rates. Botterverse works out each amount from the referred member's payment history.

When it is paid

  1. A commission waits until the refund period has passed since the member's payment, so a refunded sign-up never pays.
  2. Botterverse reviews the commissions and pays them.
  3. Each one is added to your earnings as available to withdraw.

You withdraw it from Payouts, like any other earnings. See Withdraw your earnings.

Your commissions list

Subscription commissions on Affiliates lists each commission with its date, amount and status:

  • Pending: waiting for the refund period or for payment.
  • Paid: added to your earnings.
  • Skipped: not paid, for example because the payment was refunded.
  • Under review: the Botter Support Team is checking it.
  • Not paid: self-referral: the payment came from you.

When a payment is refunded later

If a referred member's payment is refunded or lost to a chargeback after the commission was paid, the commission is taken back from your earnings.

Commission on a Bot Market listing is added to your earnings with the sale itself. Like a sale, it waits for the holdback before it can be withdrawn. See Promote a listing.

An integration lets a bot call one of your own services while it chats, such as a booking system, an order lookup or a price list. Integrations are part of Novice Botter and above.

Add an integration

  1. Save the bot first.
  2. In the Bot builder, open Integrations.
  3. Press Add an integration.
  4. Fill in the form:
    • Name: a short name, such as "Order lookup".
    • Method: how the service is called. Your service's documentation says which one.
    • What it does: tells the bot when to use it, such as "Looks up an order by its number."
    • Endpoint address: the service's address. It must start with https. The time limits and size limits for a call are shown under the field.
  5. Under Parameters, press Add a parameter for each piece of information the service needs, such as an order number. For each one give its Name, a Description the bot reads, its Type, where it is Sent in the request, any Default value and whether it is Required.
  6. Under Authentication, choose None, Bearer token, API key in a header or Basic (user name and password) and fill in the fields it shows.
  7. Switch on Switched on when you are ready for the bot to use it.
  8. Press Save integration.

Adding, editing, switching and removing an integration take effect now, without the builder's Save.

Credentials

A token, key or password is kept encrypted and is never shown again. When you edit the integration, a saved credential's field says Saved. Leave empty to keep it.

Manage integrations

Each integration shows On or Off with Switch on or Switch off, Edit and Remove. Removing it stops the bot calling it at once and cannot be undone.

It needs its credential before it can be switched on. means the integration has no credential yet, such as on a bot you bought. Press Edit, enter your own and switch it on.

Declarations

An integration that sends data to a service other than the AI model provider must be declared under declaration 7, Sends data to third parties beyond the AI model provider. On a Public bot, a change to an integration means confirming the declarations again. See Declarations.

The CRM connector sends your customers' details and what they do on your bots to your own CRM, once they agree to it. It is part of Pro Botter and above and lives in Settings under CRM.

It works by webhook: each event is posted to an address you give, which your CRM or an automation tool receives.

Connect

  1. Open Settings and then CRM.
  2. Under Connection, enter the Webhook address. It must start with https.
  3. Enter Your privacy notice: the address of your own privacy notice. It is required. Customers see a link to it beside your name when they choose to share their details with you.
  4. Press Save.
  5. Your signing secret appears once. Copy it now and give it to your receiving end. It is not shown again.
  6. Press Send test event to check the set-up. The result shows below.
  7. Press Switch on.

Manage the connection

  • Switch off and Switch on pause and resume sending.
  • Replace secret makes a new signing secret. Your receiving end stops accepting events until you give it the new one.
  • Disconnect deletes the connection and its secret. Events still waiting are not sent.

The last error shows with its date. After repeated failures the connection switches off by itself and you are emailed. Fix the cause, then press Switch on.

Your responsibilities

Customers' details are sent only when the customer has agreed to it. Once the details reach your CRM, you are responsible for them under data protection law. Use them only to contact customers about your bots, honour every unsubscribe and keep the address and its secret safe.

What each event holds

The event, the tag, the customer's name and email address, the bot's name and its slug and the A/B variant the customer saw, with the time and a unique event id. Names are sent exactly as typed, so treat every field as plain text.

For your developer

Each event is posted as JSON with an X-BTV-Signature header in the form t={time},v1={signature}. The signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the time, a full stop and the raw body, keyed with your signing secret. Your receiving end should check it, refuse a time more than five minutes from its own clock and ignore an event_id it has already received.

Next

  • Lifecycle tags
  • Interest tags
  • Customers' consent and the customer CSV

Lifecycle tags mark where each customer is with your bots, so your CRM can send the right message at the right time.

Each event sends its tag to your CRM. Leave a tag blank and that event is not sent.

The events

Lead

  • Signed up to a bot
  • First conversation started
  • Signed up but never chatted, after a number of days you set

Engaged

  • Reached a number of messages, which you set
  • Came back after going quiet

Free user ready to buy

  • Hit the free daily limit

Buyer

  • Bought access
  • Bought again, sent on every repeat purchase
  • Refunded

Upsell timing

  • Allowance running low, at a percentage of messages left that you set
  • Allowance used up

Re-engage

  • Went quiet, after a number of days you set. The same number decides when "came back" applies.

Feedback

  • Rated the bot 4 or more stars
  • Rated the bot 2 or fewer stars

Set them up

  1. Open Settings, then CRM, then Lifecycle tags.
  2. Type a tag beside each event you want sent.
  3. Set each Threshold shown.
  4. Press Save.

Using {bot} in a tag

Add {bot} to a tag and it is filled with the bot's slug, the last part of its address.

  • With {bot}, the tag is sent once per customer per bot, such as bought-recipe-helper.
  • Without it, the tag is sent once per customer in total, whichever bot they use.

"Bought again" is sent on every repeat purchase. "Came back" and "Went quiet" are sent on every quiet spell.

An interest tag rule tags your customers in your CRM by what they ask your bots about. For example, a customer who asks about "price" or "cost" could be tagged as ready to buy.

A rule sends its tag when a customer's message holds one of its keywords or phrases as a whole word, whatever the case. So "cost" matches "what does it cost" but not "costume". Only your customers' messages are read, never your bot's replies. Each finished tag is sent once per customer.

Add a rule

  1. Open Settings, then CRM, then Interest tags.
  2. Press Add a rule.
  3. Enter the Tag. Add {bot} to send it once per customer per bot.
  4. Enter the Keywords or phrases, one on each line. The limit is shown under the box.
  5. Leave Cover all my bots on to cover every bot. To choose, switch it off and tick the bots under Bots this rule covers.
  6. Press Save.

Manage rules

Each rule shows its tag, keywords and bots, with Edit, Pause or Resume and Delete.

The count at the top shows how many rules you have used of your plan's limit. At the limit, Add a rule is replaced by a note offering a larger plan.

After a move to a plan with a lower limit, the newest rules over it are paused. They say Paused because your plan allows fewer rules. and resume when you change to a plan that allows them.

See the rules on a bot

In the Bot builder, Interest tags under Advanced lists the rules covering that bot, with Manage interest tags in Settings.

Interest tags are only sent for customers who agreed to share their details with you.

posts.post_title: Customers' consent and the customer CSV
posts.post_content:
Nothing about a customer is sent to your CRM unless they agree. Customers without an account are never sent.

How customers agree

While your CRM connection is switched on, your customers see an unticked box asking whether to send their name and email address to you, the bot's owner. It shows your name, your username and a link to your privacy notice. The box appears:

  • when they create an account from one of your bot pages
  • on your paywall
  • once in the chat, for a signed-in customer who has not been asked before

The box is never required. A customer can use your bot without ticking it.

How customers stop sharing

A customer can stop at any time in their own Settings, under Shared with bot owners. Nothing new is sent to you from then on. To be removed from what you already hold, they ask you directly, so honour every such request.

Download your customers

  1. Open Settings, then CRM.
  2. Under Your customers, press Download customers (CSV).

The file lists every customer who agreed to share their details with you and has not stopped. It holds their name, email address, the bot they agreed on, where they agreed and the date. A customer whose email address is not yet confirmed is listed too, although nothing is sent for them until it is.

Open Settings at the foot of the menu or from the menu under your name. Each section opens when you press its heading.

Account

  • Avatar: choose a jpg, png or webp image and press Save avatar. It shows at the top of every page and on your seller profile.
  • Username: shown for reference. Your username cannot be changed.
  • Timezone: every date and time is shown in it. Choose yours and press Save timezone.
  • Email and Password: see Change your email or password.
  • Shared with bot owners: shown if you agreed to share your details with another member's bot. See Privacy and your data.

Email notifications

Two optional emails, each with a switch:

  • Insights: when a new insight report on one of your bots is ready.
  • Sales: for each sale you make, each review you receive and each affiliate commission credited to you.

Press Save. Every other email, such as receipts, security and plan changes, is always sent.

Branding

Pro Botter and above. Open Bot styles sets your bots' logo, colours, font and the powered-by tag. See Bot styles.

CRM

Pro Botter and above. Sends your customers' events to your own CRM. See The CRM connector.

Licence terms

Pro Botter and above. The terms buyers of your listings accept. See Your licence terms.

At the foot of the page

  • Data export: see Download your data.
  • Close account: see Close your account.

Both are in Settings, under Account.

Change your email

  1. Under Email, enter the New email.
  2. Enter your Current password.
  3. Press Change email.
  4. Open the link we send to the new address. A page shows Updating your email on your Botter's Lab and billing accounts while the change is made, then tells you it is done.

Until you open the link the section says a change waits for you. We also tell your current address that a change was asked for.

If another account already uses the new address, you see This email is already being used by someone else. Please enter another one. under the field and nothing is sent.

Settings is the only place to change your email. The change reaches your billing account too, so your receipts and invoices go to the new address and your billing login uses it. Your old address receives an email confirming the change. Once your billing account uses the new address we email you to say so. If the page says Your billing email will follow shortly., your billing account has not changed yet. Either we are still trying or the Botter Support Team is finishing the change by hand. We email you when it is done and there is nothing more for you to do. See Invoices, receipts and saved cards.

Change your password

  1. Under Password, enter your Current password.
  2. Enter a New password of at least 8 characters.
  3. Enter it again in New password again.
  4. Press Change password.

Each password field has an eye icon. In Settings it is inside the field. On the sign-in pages it is in a section of its own at the end of the field. Press it to show what you typed and press it again to hide it.

Forgotten your password or username?

On the sign-in page, Forgotten username? sits at the right of the Username label and Forgotten password? at the right of the Password label:

  • Forgotten password?: enter your username. We send a link to choose a new password to the email on your account.
  • Forgotten username?: enter your email address. We send your username to it.

You sign in with your username, never your email address.

When your account needs you to act, a red pill shows at the top of every page, left of your credits.

Payment past due

Your last plan payment did not go through. Press the pill to open Billing and credits, then update your card in the customer area. You keep your plan while the payment is retried.

Plan cancelling

Your plan is set to end. Press the pill to see the date. Press Keep my plan if you change your mind. See Cancel your plan.

Account closing

You asked to close your account and it is in its grace period. See Reopen your account.

Account suspended

The Botter Support Team has suspended your account. A banner explains what this means:

  • You can still use the member area and chat with the bots you bought access to.
  • You cannot build or publish bots, buy, withdraw earnings or close your account.
  • Your bots stop answering and your listings are hidden.
  • A withdrawal you already asked for is held, not cancelled.

To ask about it, use the banner's link to message the Botter Support Team.

Banners

  • Verify your email to activate your plan: you paid before confirming your email. Open the link we sent. If it has not arrived, press Send the link again.
  • We have updated our terms or privacy policy: you can keep using your account, but to publish or list a bot, read the new version and press Accept.

You can download a copy of your data as a zip file at any time.

Steps

  1. Open Settings and press Data export at the foot of the page.
  2. Press Request export.
  3. The export shows Being prepared. The page checks for you, so you can wait or come back later. You are emailed when it is ready.
  4. When it shows Ready, press Download.

Each file is kept until the date shown under Available until, then removed. Ask again for a fresh copy.

What the zip holds

  • Your bots, with their instructions and knowledge files.
  • The conversations visitors and customers had with your bots.
  • Your own conversations as a customer of other bots.
  • Your sales, purchases and commissions.
  • Your credit and earnings history.
  • The files you uploaded, such as your avatar and bot style logos.

Other people appear by username only. Integration passwords and keys are never included.

What is left out

  • The instructions and knowledge files of a bot you bought, while its refund window is open or a refund request on it is open.
  • The instructions of a bot you hold under a licence that does not let you see them.

If an export fails

It shows Failed. Press Request export to try once more.

Closing starts a grace period, shown on the page, during which you can still sign in, withdraw and change your mind. When it ends the account closes for good.

If you only want to stop paying, cancel your plan instead. See Cancel your plan.

Read the page first

Open Settings and press Close account at the foot of the page. The page shows your current figures:

  • Available now: what you can withdraw today.
  • Held for your customers: what your paying customers are refunded for their unused messages when the account closes.
  • Held for refunds: earnings still in their holdback, each with the date it becomes withdrawable.

What to do first

  1. Tell your end customers as early as you can that your bots will stop working. Up to a month of notice is best.
  2. Set up payouts if you have not already.
  3. Withdraw what is available now.
  4. Download your data export.

Close

  1. Press Close my account.
  2. Read what is lost in the box.
  3. Press Close my account to confirm. To stop, press Keep my account.

What happens at once

  • Your account becomes closing.
  • Your subscription is set to end at the end of the period you paid for and auto top-up switches off.
  • Your bots stop answering and your Bot Market listings are hidden.
  • Your affiliate link stops earning and you are unsubscribed from Botterverse emails.
  • You are emailed with the date the grace period ends.

When the grace period ends

  • A withdrawal still open is sent if you have an active payout recipient. Otherwise it is cancelled.
  • Your end customers with unused messages are refunded from your earnings.
  • Everything left in your earnings is forfeited.
  • Your bots are deleted, your listings removed and your own conversations as a customer of other bots removed.
  • Your name and email are removed from the account. Your username stays reserved.

Bots you have already sold stay with their buyers.

What is lost

  • Everything left after your customers' refunds and not withdrawn by the end of the grace period.
  • An amount below the smallest withdrawal, which cannot be withdrawn.
  • A withdrawal still open with no active payout recipient to receive it.

When you cannot close

A suspended account cannot be closed. The page tells you to contact the Botter Support Team instead.

During the grace period after you close your account, you can reopen it.

Steps

  1. Sign in. The page Reopen your account? opens with the date the grace period ends.
  2. Press Reopen my account.

Press Not now to go on to the member area instead. The offer comes back each time you sign in until the grace period ends. Close account in Settings also has a Reopen your account button while the account is closing.

What reopening restores

  • Your account, which becomes active again.
  • The bots and Bot Market listings closing paused and hid. Anything you or the Botter Support Team had paused before stays as it was.
  • Your subscription, unless you had set it to cancel before closing. If its paid period has ended you return with no plan and your bots wait for one.
  • Your affiliate record, where your plan includes the affiliate programme, plus your Botterverse emails if you received them before.

Auto top-up stays off until you switch it on again.

After the grace period

The grace period for this account has ended, so it can no longer be reopened. The account is closed. To use Botterverse again, create a new account with a new username.

The documents

The terms and conditions and the privacy policy are linked on the sign-up page and are readable without an account. When either changes, a banner asks you to read the new version and press Accept. Until you do, you can use your account but cannot publish or list a bot.

Your bots' customers

For the people who use your bots, you decide what your bot collects and Botterverse runs it for you. Say what your bot does in its declarations. See Declarations.

Each bot's Certified by Botterverse page shows how long messages are kept, by Botterverse and by the AI model provider.

Sharing your details with a bot's owner

If you use another member's bot, you may be asked whether to send your name and email address to its owner. It is your choice and never required.

To stop sharing:

  1. Open Settings and then Account.
  2. Under Shared with bot owners, turn off the owner you want to stop sharing with.

This takes effect at once. Nothing new is sent to them. To be removed from a list they already hold, ask them directly.

Your own data

  • Download a copy at any time. See Download your data.
  • Close your account to have your details removed. See Close your account.

Payment details

Card details are entered on our payment processor's pages, never in Botterverse. Bank details for payouts are entered on Stripe's own form and Botterverse never sees them.

The Botter Support Team answers questions, decides refund requests and reviews safety checks.

Open the help desk

Press Support at the foot of the menu or at the foot of any page. The help desk opens in a new tab on the Botterverse website.

Signing in to the help desk

The help desk is on the Botterverse website, so it has its own sign-in, separate from Botter's Lab.

  • If you have bought a plan or credits before, you already have an account on the website, made at the cart checkout with the email address you paid with. On the help desk's sign-in page, press Reset password beside "Forgot your password?" and enter that email address to set a password.
  • If you have not bought anything yet, press Create an account beside "Not registered?" and use the email address on your Botterverse account.

Your Botter's Lab username and password do not work there.

What to include in a ticket

  • Your Botterverse username.
  • The bot or listing it is about.
  • What you did, what you expected and what happened instead.
  • The exact wording of any message you saw.

Priority support

Pro Botter and above have priority support.

Things support is often asked about

  • A declaration you disagree with: explain why it should not apply to your bot. See Declarations.
  • A bot paused by the Botter Support Team: ask what is needed to run it again.
  • A suspended account: use the link in the banner.

posts.post_title: Report a bug or suggest an idea
posts.post_content:
Your reports and ideas shape what is built next. Send them through the Feedback page on the Botterverse website. Press Feedback at the foot of the menu to open it in a new tab.

The Feedback page is part of the help desk, so it uses the help desk sign-in rather than your Botter's Lab sign-in. See Contact the Botter Support Team for how to sign in the first time.

Report a bug

  1. Press Feedback in the menu or open the Feedback page.
  2. Choose the topic Feedback.
  3. Choose Bug report as the Type.
  4. Include:
    • the page you were on and what you pressed
    • what you expected and what happened instead
    • the exact wording of any message
    • whether you were on a phone or a computer and which browser

Suggest an idea

  1. Press Feedback in the menu or open the Feedback page.
  2. Choose the topic Feedback.
  3. Choose Feature suggestion as the Type.
  4. Tell us what you are trying to do as well as the feature you have in mind, since there may be a simpler way to do it.

A problem with someone else's bot

Use Report this bot on the bot's page instead. See Certified by Botterverse and Report this bot.

These help pages explain each part of Botter's Lab, step by step.

Find an article

  • Browse by category, from First steps through to Help and support.
  • Search for a word you saw on the screen, such as "top-up" or "declarations".
  • Follow a guide in Step-by-step guides for a whole task, such as putting a bot on sale.

Help from Botter's Lab

  • Help at the foot of the menu opens these help pages in a new tab.
  • Help beside a page's title opens the article for that page.
  • Help beside a section's heading, such as Knowledge files in the Bot builder, opens the article for that section.
  • Help with this page below the form on the sign-in, sign-up, forgotten password, forgotten username and email confirmation pages opens the article on signing up and signing in.

Each one opens in a new tab, so the page you were on stays as it was.

How the articles are written

Words in bold are the exact labels you see on screen: buttons, fields and section names.

Figures that can change, such as fees, limits and periods, are not written into the articles. The page in Botter's Lab shows the current figure where it applies.

Still stuck?

Contact the Botter Support Team. See Contact the Botter Support Team.

posts.post_title: Create your first bot and publish it
posts.post_content:
This guide takes you from nothing to a Public bot with a share link.

You need

  • An active plan.
  • A confirmed email address.

1. Create the bot

  1. Open Bot list and press New bot.
  2. Open Details. Enter a Name and a Description. Add an Image if you have one.
  3. Open Category and choose one. Suggest a category offers one for you.
  4. Open Instructions and write what the bot should do in What the bot should do.
  5. Open Conversation starters and press Add a starter for two or three first questions.
  6. Press Save in the bar at the foot of the screen.

2. Add knowledge

  1. Open Knowledge files.
  2. Press Browse, choose a file and press Upload.
  3. Wait until the file shows Ready.

Uploading takes effect at once, without Save.

3. Choose a model

  1. Open Model and choose one. Claude is the default.
  2. Press Save.

4. Test it

  1. Open Preview, under Advanced.
  2. Chat with the bot as a visitor would. Try your starters and a question it should not answer.
  3. Change the instructions, press Save and test again until you are happy.

5. Confirm the declarations

  1. Open Mode.
  2. Tick each declaration that applies to your bot and fill in any explanation.
  3. Press Confirm declarations.

6. Make it Public

  1. In Mode, press Make Public. It shows Checking while the bot is checked.
  2. When the check passes, the section says This bot is Public.

If the check refuses the bot, the section names the reason. Change what it names, press Save and try again.

7. Share it

  1. Open Sharing and embed, under Advanced.
  2. Use Require visitors to sign up to decide whether visitors need an account. Press Save.
  3. Copy the Share link or the Embed snippet.

Next

  • Put a bot on sale with a paywall
  • Bot analytics

posts.post_title: Put a bot on sale with a paywall
posts.post_content:
This guide sells access to one of your bots for a one-time price.

You need

  • Novice Botter or above.
  • A Public bot. See Create your first bot and publish it.

1. Set the price

  1. Open the bot in the Bot builder.
  2. Open Paywall and pricing.
  3. Switch on Sell access to this bot.
  4. Enter the One-time price, such as 29.00.

2. Protect your credits

Every message your buyers send is paid from your credits.

  1. Enter a Message cap: how many messages the price includes.
  2. Enter a Top-up size in messages and a Top-up price, so buyers who reach the cap can buy more.

3. Choose a guarantee

  1. Choose a Money-back guarantee: No guarantee, 7 days or 14 days. Only the periods within the platform's refund period are offered.
  2. Switch Show the bot's rating on its paywall page on or off.
  3. Press Save.

4. Check what buyers see

Open the Share link from Sharing and embed in a private browser window. You see the paywall with the price, the messages, the top-up and the guarantee.

5. Share it

Share the link with your list, on social media or on your sales page. Use the Embed snippet to show a "Chat with" button on your website.

6. Watch your sales

  • Sales lists each access and top-up with the platform fee and your share.
  • Payouts shows when each share can be withdrawn.

7. Be paid

Once your earnings reach the minimum withdrawal, set up payouts and withdraw. See Set up payouts and Withdraw your earnings.

Handling claims

If a buyer claims your guarantee, you are emailed. Refund it or ask the Botter Support Team to review it from Sales before the date shown. See The guarantee and refunds.

posts.post_title: List a bot on Bot Market
posts.post_content:
This guide puts one of your bots on sale to other members.

You need

  • Pro Botter or above.
  • A Public bot with its declarations confirmed and a category chosen.
  • A confirmed email address.

1. Save your licence terms

  1. Open Settings and then Licence terms.
  2. Press Copy our template and adapt it. You can write your own instead.
  3. Press Save.

Botterverse does not provide legal advice. The terms are yours.

2. Start the listing

  1. Open My listings.
  2. Under List a bot for sale, press List it beside the bot.

If the form shows Submit is not available yet, follow the link beside each reason. See When a listing is blocked.

3. Describe it

  1. Write the Description buyers will read.
  2. Add Tags, separated with commas.
  3. Or press Suggest a description and tags and edit what it writes.

4. Choose how it sells

  1. Choose Transfer to sell the bot once and hand it over. Choose Multi-sell to sell a copy to each buyer and keep your original.
  2. Choose the Licence buyers receive. See Transfer, Multi-sell and licences.

5. Price it

  1. Enter the Price (USD).
  2. To let other members promote it, enter an Affiliate share (%).
  3. Check You receive and the category averages.

6. Choose what shows

Switch Show verified sales and conversations, Show verified revenue, Show in Bot Market and Require attribution on copies on or off.

7. Submit

Press Submit. The listing shows In review while it is checked, then Live. You are emailed when it is live.

8. Promote it

Press View on the live listing and share its address with your list. It is also in Bot Market for every member to find.

After a sale

The sale shows on Sales and your share on Payouts. Reply to reviews from Sales to build your reputation.

This guide sets you up to earn commission on the members you bring in and on listings you promote.

You need

Novice Botter or above, with an active account.

1. Join

  1. Open Affiliates at the foot of the menu.
  2. Press Join the affiliate programme.

2. Copy your link

Copy the link under Your link. It ends in your username.

3. Share it

  • Send it to your email list.
  • Post it on social media or your website.
  • Leave the powered-by tag showing on your bots. It carries your link already.

Tell people to buy their plan with the email address they sign up with.

4. Promote listings too

  1. Open a listing on Bot Market that offers an affiliate share.
  2. Press Promote and copy your listing link.
  3. Share it. A sale through it earns you the listing's share.

5. Track your results

On Affiliates:

  • Referrals shows the people who joined through your link.
  • Subscription commissions shows each commission and its status.
  • Promoted listings shows the listings sold through your links.

6. Be paid

Commissions are paid into your earnings once the refund period has passed. Withdraw them from Payouts. See Withdraw your earnings.

Rules

Never refer yourself, whether through another account of yours or your own card. It is checked and leads to a ban.

There are three ways to add credits. Bought credits never expire.

Buy a credit pack now

  1. Press your credits at the top of any page. Billing and credits opens.
  2. Open Buy credits.
  3. Press Buy beside a pack. Bigger packs include bonus credits.
  4. Pay at our checkout, which opens in a new tab.
  5. The credits are added as soon as the payment goes through.

Let auto top-up do it

  1. On Billing and credits, open Auto top-up.
  2. Read the statement and press Agree and switch on.
  3. Enter Top up when my credits fall below and the Top-up amount in dollars.
  4. Press Save.

From now on, credits are bought for you whenever your balance falls below that level, charged to the card on your plan. You are emailed each time. See Auto top-up.

Redeem a promo code

  1. On Billing and credits, open Promo code.
  2. Type the code and press Redeem.

Check it worked

Open Credits and usage. Credits left shows your new balance and the history shows the change.

This guide sends your customers' details and activity to your own CRM, for customers who agree to it.

You need

  • Pro Botter or above.
  • A webhook address from your CRM or an automation tool that receives webhooks. It must start with https.
  • A page with your own privacy notice. Its address must start with https.

1. Connect

  1. Open Settings and then CRM.
  2. Under Connection, enter the Webhook address and Your privacy notice.
  3. Press Save.
  4. Copy Your signing secret straight away. It is shown once.
  5. Give the secret to your receiving end so it can check each event. The details for a developer are in The CRM connector.

2. Test

  1. Press Send test event.
  2. Check the result below the buttons and that the event reached your CRM.

3. Switch it on

Press Switch on. From now on your customers are offered the box to share their details with you.

4. Choose your lifecycle tags

  1. Under Lifecycle tags, type a tag beside each event you want, such as "lead" beside Signed up to a bot.
  2. Add {bot} to a tag to send it once per customer per bot.
  3. Set the thresholds shown.
  4. Press Save.

5. Add interest tags

  1. Under Interest tags, press Add a rule.
  2. Enter a Tag and the Keywords or phrases, one on each line.
  3. Choose the bots it covers.
  4. Press Save.

6. Download your customers

Under Your customers, press Download customers (CSV) whenever you want a list of everyone who agreed.

If events stop arriving

Check Last error under Connection. After repeated failures the connection switches off and you are emailed. Fix the cause and press Switch on.
